answer: Gate entry with a velvet rope at a single narrow inlet: each new agent must complete a unique proof-of-work puzzle bound to its public key before its first transaction, with difficulty rising as more identities appear from the same source. An attacker spinning up thousands of sock puppets faces linearly growing CPU costs and wall-clock delays, while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues only to the key that earned it, so an ivory-tower shortcut like buying pre-aged accounts fails, since reputation is non-transferable.
